about:
Arkansas Steel Associates, LLC (ASA) was founded in 1989 as a joint venture between Yamato Kogyo and Sumitomo Corporation. The plant is located in northeast Arkansas in the town of Newport on 300 acres.

ASA manufactures merchant bar quality (MBQ) billets, hot-rolled double-shoulder railroad tie plates, and hot-rolled flat bars in various cross sections and lengths. The company operates on a 300-acre site in Newport and is described as the producer of railroad tie plates in North America. Its tie plates accommodate rail sizes from 115RE to 140RE and meet AREMA and customer specifications; all products meet Buy America requirements.

The company serves customers ranging from small contractors to Class 1 railroads, supplying tie plates and flat bars for railroad infrastructure projects. Its products are used in North American rail networks and meet Buy America provisions for federally funded projects.

ASA emphasizes quality and environmental management, holding ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 14001:2015 certifications, as well as AAR M-1003 and GSCC-SBET certifications. The company has published a decarbonization plan targeting zero Scope 2 emissions from its electric furnaces.

name: Arkansas Truck Center
old_description: The trucking industry has changed dramatically in recent years. Equipment is far more sophisticated and expensive than we would have imagined just a few years ago. We have over 30 acres of late model inventory. We warehouse over 13,000 square feet of new, used and remanufactured parts for local pickup or worldwide shipping.
about:
Arkansas Truck Center operates from Alma, Arkansas, where it has built a family-owned business around heavy-duty truck parts and recovery services. The company does not disclose its founding year or the names of its founders, but it describes itself as a pacesetter in the region with a commitment to modern equipment and trained personnel.

The facility spans more than 30 acres of late-model truck inventory and includes a 13,000-square-foot warehouse stocked with new, used, and remanufactured parts for brands such as Peterbilt and Freightliner. In addition to parts distribution, the company provides wrecker recovery services and purchases trucks coast to coast for resale, export, scrap, or parts reclamation.

Customers range from local fleets picking up parts at the warehouse to international buyers served by worldwide shipping. The business serves the commercial trucking industry, heavy-duty recovery operators, and export markets, offering both component supply and complete vehicle acquisition.

Arkansas Truck Center says its differentiation lies in the combination of a large on-hand inventory, a family-owned structure that emphasizes personal service, and the ability to handle everything from single-part orders to whole-fleet purchases.

old_description: We are a family owned and operated business. We have been at our current location since 1964. Our business was founded by my father Fred Philippus. I have been involved with the company since 1965. My wife and I have owned the company since 1985.
about:
Arrow Sheet Metal Works, Inc. operates from Tampa, Florida, where it has been located since 1964. The company was founded in 1952 by Fred Philippus and remains family-owned; his son Bob Philippus has been involved since 1965 and, together with his wife, has owned the business since 1985.

The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication, working with stainless steel, aluminum, steel, galvanized steel, brass, and copper. Capabilities include welding, grinding, polishing, pipe bending up to 2-inch diameter, and shearing and bending materials up to 1/2-inch thick. They produce a range of custom items such as countertops, handrails, brackets, platforms, frames, stands, kitchen hood shells, shelving, racks, panels, cabinets, truck boxes, light brackets, and transition fittings. Field installation and portable welding services are also offered, and local delivery is handled with company-owned pickup trucks and a flatbed.

The customer base spans commercial and residential clients throughout the Tampa Bay area. Notable accounts include Tampa Electric Company, Busch Gardens/SeaWorld, Southern Wine and Spirits, Tampa International Airport, Outback Steakhouse, McDonald’s, Hanna Bartoletta Homes, Hillsborough County, and the City of Tampa.

The company emphasizes that no job is too big or too small, building a reputation for going above and beyond on projects that require specialized fabrication not available off the shelf.

old_description: Photovoltaic solar systems absorb and convert the sunlight into electricity. about:
Atlas Metal Works LLC operates as a custom metal fabrication house in South Windsor, Connecticut. The company is certified as a Small Business Enterprise by the Connecticut Department of Administrative Services (CT DAS).

The shop provides a range of metalworking services including laser cutting, high-definition plasma cutting, shearing, press-brake forming, CNC punching, plate and pipe rolling, polishing, sawing, and multiple welding processes (MIG/flux-core, TIG, aluminum MIG, spot, and stud welding). Key equipment includes a BLM LS5 12 kW plate laser capable of cutting 5-by-10-foot plates up to one inch thick, a Vectis UR20 cobot welder with 48-inch reach, AccurPress brakes (320-ton and 175-ton), an AccurShear, a Euromac 55-ton CNC punch, a Timesaver 8-inch stainless polisher, Hypertherm and Thermadyne plasma systems, and a Marvel 18-inch automated saw. The company also sells raw stock—sheet, plate, angle, flats, and channel—in full lengths or cut to size, and accepts design files in AutoCAD, FastCAM, or FastSHAPES formats, offering design assistance when needed.

Atlas Metal Works serves commercial clients such as OEM manufacturers, general contractors, construction firms, and other fabrication houses that lack in-house capacity. Its work spans residential, commercial, and industrial projects, with materials including stainless steel, aluminum, carbon steel, galvanized steel, brass, copper, bronze, and mild steel.

The business positions itself as a gap-filler for manufacturers needing supplemental shearing, bending, laser cutting, welding, and hole-punching capacity, emphasizing complete project execution from design through finished delivery.

about:
Atlas Wire, LLC was founded in 1966 in Itasca, Illinois, and has served the electronic, OEM, and distribution markets for over five decades. The privately held company operates a second production facility in Tucson, Arizona, and is led by President and CEO Bruce Leska.

The company manufactures PVC, cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE), and nylon insulated electrical lead wires in single- and multi-conductor constructions, covering more than 4,900 distinct wire types in sizes ranging from 4 to 30 AWG. Value-added services include spiral striping, extruded longitudinal lines, twisting, heat bonding, respooling, and custom drum or spool packaging. Both facilities maintain tooling for longitudinal line applications, with the Itasca plant offering up to 40% coverage and Tucson up to 30%.

Atlas Wire supplies automotive low-voltage battery cable and primary wire, UL-recognized appliance wire, 600-volt machine tool wire, PVC-insulated building and fixture wire, and military-specification hookup wire for electronic equipment. Its customer base spans original equipment manufacturers, distributors, and the broader electronics sector, with products meeting UL, CSA, automotive, and military standards.

The company describes itself as service-oriented, emphasizing the lowest minimum order quantities, short production lead times, and a willingness to accommodate special requirements. Its quality policy commits to continual improvement, on-time delivery of defect-free products, and compliance with ISO 9001 and IATF 16949:2016.

Averra Packaging operates from West Valley City, Utah. The company traces its roots to 1989, when it began thermoforming out of a garage. Today it runs a 40,000-square-foot sterile healthcare packaging design and manufacturing facility.

Its process covers design and development, in-house prototyping that delivers true thermoformed samples in days, a Bridge Tooling™ step for production-equivalent parts, in-house tooling via its own machine shop, and full-scale production. Averra serves the medical device and consumer goods industries. Its medical customers include companies developing life-altering devices that require sterile barrier systems, while its consumer division focuses on high-quality retail packaging. The firm also acts as a manufacturer of record, combining packaging expertise with regulatory documentation under one roof.

The company says it was driven by a purpose to deliver smart, effective packaging that meets modern business demands, emphasizing that the only barrier between a device and patient outcomes should be a sterile one. It highlights sustainable practices: 75 percent of materials contain recycled content, one million pounds of post-production waste are recycled annually, and 96 percent of its products are recyclable.

Azuma Foods International Inc. USA (AFI) was founded in 1990 and is headquartered in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The company operates as a privately held importer and processor of Japanese-inspired seafood and plant-based foods, though its ownership structure and founders are not publicly disclosed.

AFI produces a range of products including Tobikko (flying fish roe), Masago (capelin roe), dry toppings, seaweed salad, calamari salad, sushi-grade items, appetizers, fry-and-grill offerings, and plant-based alternatives. The company maintains an in-house laboratory equipped with PCR thermal cyclers and ELISA testing systems for microbiological and chemical analysis, and operates under a HACCP-based quality management system that covers hazard analysis, sanitation standard operating procedures, allergen control, gluten testing, and a Foreign Supplier Verification Program. All foreign suppliers must provide HACCP plans and certificates of compliance aligned with FDA guidelines.

The company serves the food service industry, supplying distributors, restaurants, and retail accounts such as Costco, which audits AFI under its GMP program. AFI’s Sea Salad brand, featuring award-winning calamari salad and seaweed salad, has been recognized as a 2020 Seafood Excellence Awards finalist for its Island Style Marinated Ogo Seaweed.

AFI’s founding mission is to achieve an “Assimilation of Food Culture to the World” by blending traditional Japanese cuisine with global food traditions. The company emphasizes sustainable, vegetarian-friendly products with no added colors, and differentiates itself through its in-house laboratory capabilities, stringent supplier verification, and ongoing pursuit of SQF certification.

From our 6,000 square foot facility in the early 1990’s, we upgraded to our current home, which has provided us with 84,000 square feet of state-of-the-art welding and fabrication space since 2007. Our facility allows us to compete not only regionally and nationally, but also internationally. We’re focused on providing customers worldwide with high-quality RPE and RPP liners, tarps and covers.
about:
BTL Liners operates from an 84,000-square-foot fabrication facility in Prineville, Oregon. The company traces its roots to 1981 when Ron Perlatti founded Bend Tarp & Liner in nearby Bend, initially installing pond liners before partnering with a Japanese firm to develop heavyweight reinforced polyethylene liners. Ownership passed to Perlatti's son Brad and his wife Jan in 1997, and in 2021 their daughter Chelsea and her husband Travis Wilcox took over, marking the third generation of family leadership.

The company manufactures custom geomembrane liners, covers, and tarps using reinforced polyethylene (RPE), reinforced polypropylene (RPP), and low-density polyethylene (LDPE). Its Prineville plant houses welding and fabrication equipment capable of producing single panels up to 150,000 square feet, supported by a team of 20-plus technicians. BTL also provides installation assistance worldwide, either onsite or remotely.

BTL serves agriculture, aquaponics, energy, golf courses, greenhouses, irrigation, landfill, mining, and water-feature markets. Project examples include cable wake-board parks in California and Ohio, a 40-acre irrigation reservoir in the western U.S., frac-tank insulated covers, a coal mine in British Columbia, and custom truck and boat tarps shipped globally.

The business began after Perlatti identified a need for a stronger, lighter alternative to HDPE, PVC, and EPDM liners. The resulting double-scrim RPE material can be prefabricated and installed quickly, offering a cost-effective solution. BTL's stated mission is to give clients confidence that its containment systems exceed requirements for resource conservation and control.

name: BY DESIGN Furniture & Interior Design
old_description: Influenced by traditional design elements, this spring's trends are founded on a desire for spaces that feel both timeless and grounded. The newest pieces seem to balance refinement and naturalism through the use of detailed accents, botanical motifs, organic...
about:
BY DESIGN Furniture & Interior Design operates from a showroom in Clive, Iowa, a suburb of Des Moines. The business traces its roots to December 1976 when Russell and Ruthann Clark helped their son Kevin and daughter-in-law Bonita open Wood Stock Ltd., a store dedicated to unfinished wood furniture in Des Moines. The current BY DESIGN entity was established in 1998 after the Clarks merged their wood specialty store with an upholstery concept called Sofas by Design. The company remains family-owned and describes itself as a locally owned small business.

The firm combines a retail showroom with a full-service interior design studio. Its designers — degreed professionals — help clients specify customizable furniture sourced from vendors such as American Leather, Four Hands, Norwalk Furniture, and BDI. The showroom features a fabric wall stocked with thousands of fabrics and leathers, and dining tables can be ordered in wood, tile, stone, or glass tops with various finishes. The company also offers furniture restoration services and a furniture protection plan.

BY DESIGN serves residential clients throughout the Des Moines metro area and also partners with outside designers through a to-the-trade program. Its customer base includes homeowners furnishing living rooms, dining rooms, bedrooms, home offices, and outdoor spaces. The company’s portfolio includes projects ranging from single-room refreshes to whole-home designs.

The Clarks founded the business on a mission to listen, inform, and inspire clients who view their homes as a focal point of their lives. The company emphasizes that it does not impose a signature style but instead helps each client discover a personal aesthetic through highly customizable product options and one-on-one design consultation.

name: Baker Medical, Inc.
old_description: is a locally-owned and operated medical supply store based in Conway, Arkansas. For more than 10 years, we've been helping individuals and healthcare professionals from all over the state of Arkansas care for themselves and their patients by offering medical supplies and equipment.
about:
Baker Medical, Inc. operates as a locally owned medical supply retailer in Conway, Arkansas, with a second location in Clinton. The company has served the state for nearly two decades, though a precise founding year is not published. It began as a neighborhood store focused on providing medical equipment and supplies directly to patients and healthcare providers across Arkansas.

The business stocks and ships a range of home healthcare products, including CPAP and BiPAP systems, catheters, incontinence supplies, diabetic and insulin pump accessories, and oral supplements. A respiratory therapist on staff performs daily CPAP setups, and the company runs a resupply program that mails fresh consumables to patients’ doors. Orders over $20 ship free via USPS, with processing within one business day and delivery in one to three days anywhere in Arkansas. The two storefronts serve as both retail counters and service centers.

Customers include individual patients managing chronic conditions at home as well as clinics and home health agencies that refer patients for equipment and ongoing supply management. The company bills most insurance plans with a valid prescription, positioning itself as an intermediary between prescribers, payers, and end users.

Baker Medical emphasizes its clinical support—particularly the respiratory therapist-led CPAP setups—and its Arkansas-focused logistics as key differentiators. The ownership describes the mission as improving patients’ quality of life through accessible equipment and responsive service.

about:
Bald Ridge Enterprises operates from Cody, Wyoming, where it was founded nearly four decades ago as a small local shop built on family values. The company is registered as a Women-Owned Small Business with the U.S. federal government and has grown into a regional contractor serving Wyoming and Montana.

The company provides complete metal construction services, specializing in architectural sheet metal fabrication and installation. Its in-house shop produces pre-manufactured steel buildings, metal roofing systems, siding, soffits, fascia, gutters, downspouts, and specialty items such as snow bars, chimney caps, and custom planter boxes. A carpentry division adds wood detailing to projects. All components are designed, fabricated, and installed by the company's own crews, giving it control over quality from start to finish.

Bald Ridge serves commercial, agricultural, residential, institutional, and government customers across the two-state area. Projects range from personal shops and farm structures to large-scale institutional and government facilities. The company's online design tool allows clients to configure building layouts and request quotes remotely.

The firm differentiates itself by building to the Architectural Sheet Metal Manual, the industry's highest standard, and by engineering its systems for the extreme weather of Wyoming and Montana. It backs its work with a standard one-year warranty plus extended manufacturer guarantees, and emphasizes a family-focused culture that has retained a certified, insured team for nearly 40 years.

name: Barku Plastics
old_description: Barku has been producing high-quality plastic parts for 40 years. Precision parts using injection molding technology as well as profiles and pipes using extrusion processes are manufactured quickly and reliably.
about:
Barku Plastics operates from Cleveland, Tennessee. The company traces its roots to 1977 when Egon Schumacher founded it as a subsidiary of LUBING Maschinenfabrik GmbH in Germany. Barku Plastics L.L.C. was established in Cleveland in September 2003 as a subsidiary of Barku Kunststofftechnik GmbH, maintaining German ownership.

The company specializes in custom plastic injection molding and profile extrusion. It runs more than 50 injection molding machines ranging from 32 to 1,100 tons, and over 10 extrusion lines capable of diameters up to 6 inches and profile widths up to 39 3/8 inches. Processes include two-component and insert molding, as well as co-extrusion for multi-material products. The facility operates three shifts and processes more than 14,000 tons of raw material annually. Materials processed include PP, PE, PS, PVC, POM, ABS, PU, and PA. Barku also provides assembly services, engineering support, mold development, and packaging of multi-part assemblies.

Barku serves customers worldwide across various industries, though specific sectors are not named in the input. The company works with clients needing precision injection-molded parts and extruded profiles and pipes, offering development, design, series production, and further processing.

Barku emphasizes flexibility, know-how, and a commitment to high quality standards, reflected in its ISO 9001:2015 certification with TUV Rheinland. The company highlights its partnerships with mold builders on three continents and continuous optimization of production processes through machine park renewal and employee training.

name: Barrett Petfood
old_description: Barrett Petfood was founded on a simple promise: If we wouldn’t feed it to our own pets, you won’t find it in our products. We help pets and pet food companies thrive by delivering a premium manufacturing and brand services experience that takes pet food from idea to bowl with integrity.
about:
Barrett Petfood is headquartered in Brainerd, Minnesota. The company was founded in 2006 when agricultural entrepreneur Mike Barrett purchased a piece of equipment intended for agricultural manufacturing, only to discover it was suited for food production. Mike and his children, Tom and Sarah Barrett, pivoted the business into pet food, with Mike later transitioning ownership to his children while continuing to supply ingredients from his farm. The company remains family-owned.

Barrett operates two facilities in central Minnesota: the original Brainerd plant and a second site opened in 2020 in Little Falls that added 160,000 square feet and two production lines. The company produces hundreds of formulas across super‑premium kibble, kibble‑plus, and freeze‑dried formats, using extrusion, milling, and automated packaging lines. Its capabilities span diet formulation, ingredient sourcing, processing, packaging, and distribution.

Barrett serves pet food brands ranging from emerging labels to market leaders, manufacturing diets for dogs, cats, reptiles, birds, livestock, and zoo animals. Customers rely on the company as a full‑service co‑manufacturer that handles everything from formulation to shipping.

The business was built on a simple promise: “If we wouldn’t feed it to our own pets, you won’t find it in our products.” The Barretts emphasize a relationship‑based philosophy, a “Don’t Say No” innovation mindset, and rigorous, laboratory‑like food‑safety standards as their differentiators.

about:
Barth Electronics, Inc. has been headquartered in Boulder City, Nevada since 1976, when the company relocated from Ohio to support weapons testing at the Nevada Test Site. Founded in 1964, the firm began by designing and manufacturing specialized test hardware for EG&G in Las Vegas and for national laboratories.

The company designs and manufactures sub-nanosecond high-energy pulse power instrumentation, including over 100 distinct pulse power products. In 1997 its engineers developed the first commercial Transmission Line Pulser (TLP) for the electrostatic discharge (ESD) industry. Today the product line encompasses the Model 4002 TLP+ for human-body-model testing, the Model 4012 VFTLP+ for charged-device-model testing, the Model 4702 HMM+ for IEC-equivalent gun discharge testing, and a 700-series of 3 kV and 5 kV pulse generators. All ESD testing services are performed in-house at the Boulder City factory, and a rental program is offered for the Model 4002 TLP+.

Barth serves the semiconductor industry with ESD device characterization and qualification testing, while its pulse power instruments are used daily in physics and pulse-power laboratories worldwide. Historical customers include EG&G and U.S. national laboratories involved in weapons testing.

The company traces its high-reliability standards to its weapons-testing heritage: “By beating our swords into plowshares, weapons testing hardware was changed into the development and manufacture of the highest quality ESD test equipment available today.” It continues to investigate new technologies for ESD and high-voltage pulse power as needs emerge.

name: Base Power Company
old_description: Base Power is an Austin, Texas-based company that designs, assembles, and deploys home battery backup systems while operating as a retail electric provider in Texas.
about:
Base Power Company was founded in 2023 in Austin, Texas, by CEO Zach Dell and co-founder Justin Lopas. Lopas previously led manufacturing at Anduril and worked on rockets at SpaceX, while the broader team brings experience from satellite constellation launches and early electric vehicle production. The company was born after Winter Storm Uri left millions of Texans without power for days, highlighting the grid’s fragility and rising electricity costs.

Base designs, assembles, and deploys its Core home battery backup system — a 39.2 kWh unit that provides 36 to 72 hours of whole-home backup — and operates as a retail electric provider in Texas and Illinois. The company handles battery pack assembly, in-house engineering, UL-certified testing, and runs a virtual power plant that dispatches stored energy to the grid during peak demand.

The primary customers are residential homeowners in Texas and Illinois seeking affordable backup power and fixed-rate electricity. The company also serves grid-storage and utility markets by aggregating its distributed batteries to provide grid-balancing services. Testimonials cite installations in Houston, Waxahachie, Cypress, Arlington, Saginaw, and Pflugerville.

Base positions its model as a low-cost alternative to traditional generators or solar-plus-storage, installing the battery for a $695 one-time fee plus a $19 monthly membership, with an all-in energy rate around 13.9¢/kWh. The battery is tested for -22°F to 122°F and submersion-rated to three feet, and the company says it earns revenue from grid services rather than marking up energy, allowing it to keep rates low.

Belmont employs nearly 200 people and has expanded its manufacturing and office facility in 2019 and again in 2022.

Belmont’s devices are used in hospital operating rooms, intensive care units, emergency departments, labor and delivery suites, and on military combat fields and emergency transport vehicles worldwide. The U.S. military awarded the company a five‑year contract worth up to $133 million in 2020, and group purchasing agreements are in place with Inc. and HealthTrust. The company also donated rapid infusers and portable warmers to Ukraine in 2022.

Belmont states that its differentiation lies in blending technical inspiration with an uncompromising quality standard, earning the trust of clinicians through patented electromagnetic heating technology, aluminum‑free disposables, and automatic air detection and removal features. The company holds MDSAP certification for its quality system and maintains direct operations in the United Kingdom and Germany.

Buitoni Food Company, headquartered in Danville, Virginia, traces its origins to 1827 in Sansepolcro, Tuscany, where founder Giulia Buitoni traded a family necklace for a pasta machine and sourced wheat from Puglia after a 40-day journey. Giovanni Buitoni brought the brand to New York City in 1939, establishing a U.S. presence that continues today.

The company manufactures fresh pasta, sauces, and cheeses at its Danville facility, emphasizing artisan techniques such as slow-roasting chicken, importing Italian 00 flour, and using aged DOP Parmigiano Reggiano and farm-fresh eggs. Production follows time-honored methods, though specific facility size, headcount, and output volumes are not disclosed.

Buitoni serves the retail grocery and foodservice sectors, distributing products through select retailers nationwide. Its customer base includes supermarket chains and consumers seeking authentic Italian meal solutions, with recipes and product locators provided on its website.

The brand differentiates itself through a commitment to Tuscan craftsmanship and ingredient integrity, rooted in Giulia Buitoni’s original pursuit of the finest wheat. The company states that “details matter” in every step, from flour milling to cheese selection, aiming to deliver a modern Italian masterpiece in each product.

Its customers send in underperforming parts for remanufacturing, and the company also provides new replacement components. The business focuses on automotive electronics and mechanical systems, with technical content and training resources aimed at service professionals.

The company’s founding mission was to fix what fails in the auto industry by building better parts backed by better service. Since its inception, CARDONE has operated on sustainability principles—reduce, reuse, recycle—treating remanufacturing as an environmental responsibility. This approach, combined with design improvements that address common failure points, is cited as a key differentiator. Core processes include wire drawing, enamel insulation coating (ceramic, PTFE, nylon, polyester), PTFE insulation, electroplating, flat‑ribbon production, annealing, stranding, cutting, straightening, grinding, polishing, and custom spooling. CFW operates 25 enamel coating machines and maintains an in‑house testing laboratory capable of dimensional measurement to 0.00001″ resolution (±0.00005″ accuracy), tensile testing, and resistance measurement.

CFW serves highly regulated markets including medical devices (implanted cardiac devices, neurological leads), aerospace and defense (lunar missions, satellite components), semiconductor (bonding wire, interconnects), electronics, industrial, marine, and chemical processing. Customers range from research institutions to prime contractors requiring precision wire for critical applications.

Founder Michael A. Greenelsh emphasized that the company’s real specialty is fulfilling customers’ specific needs, no matter how small or unusual. This philosophy, combined with ISO 9001‑certified quality systems and decades‑experienced staff, underpins CFW’s focus on custom solutions for demanding environments.

name: Capital Electro Circuits Inc
old_description: exceptional craftsmanship, on-time delivery, and customer-focused solutions
about:
Capital Electro Circuits Inc., based in Gaithersburg, Maryland, has been fabricating printed circuit boards since 1985. The company operates as a domestic manufacturer of rigid, flexible, and rigid‑flex PCBs, with a focus on specialty designs that fall outside standard fabrication lines.

The shop produces multilayer boards up to 16 layers, with finished thicknesses up to 1.300 inches, and offers advanced features such as blind/buried vias, edge plating, castellations, and controlled‑impedance structures. It works with a wide range of high‑frequency and high‑reliability laminates — including Rogers, Taconic, Arlon, and TMM series — and provides a full suite of surface finishes (HASL, ENIG, ENEPIG, hard gold, immersion tin/silver). In‑house capabilities cover CAM/DFM, drilling, plating, etching, LPI soldermask, legend printing, CNC routing and scoring, and electrical test (continuity/isolation up to 250 VDC).

The company serves aerospace and defense (including programs for Northrop Grumman, BAE Systems, NASA, Lockheed Martin, Honeywell, Sandia National Laboratories, Booz Allen Hamilton, and the U.S. Army), medical imaging and diagnostics, telecommunications (5G and satellite), automotive and electric‑vehicle systems, and RF/microwave applications up to 100 GHz. It emphasizes 100 % U.S.‑based production for military and avionics work.

Capital Electro Circuits differentiates itself by taking on “specialty” jobs that lack defined manufacturing methods, developing custom processes to deliver working parts on short notice. It maintains ISO 9001:2015 certification, UL recognition, RoHS compliance, ITAR registration, and a conflict‑minerals sourcing policy, and offers blanket orders with split deliveries.

about:
Capitol Iron Works operates from Gaithersburg, Maryland, in the heart of the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area. The company was founded in August 2014 by Ronald Vargas, who serves as president and co-owner. Vargas immigrated to the United States from Nicaragua in 2004 and learned welding on the job at Bethesda Iron Works, eventually earning his welding certification before launching his own venture, initially named Capitol Iron Solutions.

The shop specializes in custom ornamental and architectural metalwork, producing railings, stairs, handrails, glass and cable railings, steel fencing, balconies, canopies, and automatic gates. It works with stainless steel, aluminum, bronze, structural steel, wrought iron, and glass, offering powder-coat finishes. The 4,300-square-foot facility houses three fabrication units and a staff of 14. Project values range from $1,000 to $500,000, with revenue projected at $1.5 million for 2018.

Capitol Iron Works serves residential, commercial, and government clients across the D.C., Maryland, and Virginia region. Notable government work includes fabrication and installation of bronze railings for the Rayburn House Office Building under contract with the Architect of the Capitol, the federal agency responsible for the U.S. Capitol Complex. The company also handles restoration of historic metalwork.

Vargas attributes the firm’s rapid growth to customer service, on-time delivery, and a stable, skilled workforce—only one employee has left in four years. He emphasizes a willingness to tackle complex, challenging projects that other shops might avoid, combining fabrication, installation, and restoration under one roof.

The company focuses on healthcare informatics, providing a vendor-neutral platform that connects medical devices and clinical systems across hospital enterprises.

The company’s portfolio spans medical device integration, clinical surveillance, patient monitoring, virtual care, retrospective analytics, and clinical information systems. Its platform captures live-streaming data from over 1,200 medical devices — including measurements, settings, alarms, and waveforms — and delivers it using industry-standard protocols to more than 100 downstream systems such as electronic health records, clinical information systems, and alarm management tools. Key product lines include Philips Axon, Capsule Neuron, Capsule Vitals Stream, Chart Xpress, the Medical Device Information Platform, eCareManager, Clinical Insights Manager, Capsule Surveillance, and IntelliSpace Critical Care and Anesthesia (ICCA).

Capsule serves hospitals and health systems worldwide, with installations at organizations such as Hamilton Health Sciences in Canada, CoxHealth in the United States, and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust in the United Kingdom. Its solutions target acute care environments including intensive care units, perioperative settings, and general wards, aiming to reduce clinician burnout and improve patient outcomes through automated data capture and clinical decision support.

The company emphasizes its vendor-neutral, open ecosystem approach, which allows healthcare providers to leverage existing infrastructure while expanding capabilities incrementally. It also highlights deep clinical and operational experience, stating that its support extends beyond technology to fit workflows and enable clinical staff rather than burden them.

Carolina Farmstead serves residential customers seeking long-lasting, made-to-order furniture for everyday use. Its pieces have been featured on HGTV's 'Love It or List It,' the PBS series 'A Chef's Life,' and in Our State Magazine, reflecting a focus on the home furnishings market rather than commercial or institutional channels.

old_description: Carolina Yarn and Fabrics, LLC, based in Laurens, SC, is a leading manufacturer and principal supplier of highly engineered fabric-formed concrete erosion control and scour protection systems. These systems have been utilized for more than 40 years around the world.
about:
Carolina Yarn and Fabrics, LLC, based in Laurens, South Carolina, has been a manufacturer and principal supplier of highly engineered fabric-formed concrete erosion control and scour protection systems since the ARMORFORM® trade name was established in 1984. The company draws together teams of project managers, engineers, and production and field service managers dedicated to sustainable solutions.

The firm produces ARMORFORM® fabric-formed concrete systems, which use double-layer woven geo-textiles engineered exclusively as forms for casting concrete erosion control revetments and linings. The geo-textiles are woven from polyester and/or nylon yarns and designed with specific mechanical and hydraulic properties. Installation involves positioning the fabric forms and pumping high-strength, fine-aggregate concrete, either underwater or on dry land. By 2002, more than 50 million square feet of ARMORFORM® had been installed worldwide, including projects inside the Arctic Circle and at the Olmsted Locks and Dam on the Ohio River.

The company serves engineering firms, government agencies, and commercial clients across infrastructure, water, environment, industry, and energy sectors. Notable references include acceptance by the Mine Safety and Health Administration for mining facilities in 1993, U.S. Navy approval for underwater ballast and protection of pipelines and communication cables in 2002, and exclusive collaboration with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers on scour protection for the Olmsted Locks and Dam in 2008.

Carolina Yarn and Fabrics emphasizes engineered products, comprehensive technical support, and responsive delivery, which the company says have resulted in most projects being repeat work with long-standing clients. The focus on sustainable solutions for infrastructure, water, environment, industry, and energy underpins its approach.

It sells fish-finding and navigation units, handles professional installation, and then provides personalized training on how to operate the equipment. The service model centers on one-on-one sessions tailored to each customer’s specific unit and fishing style, whether they are new to electronics, switching brands, or seeking to fine-tune existing settings.

The primary clientele are recreational anglers and boaters in the Central Kentucky region. Customers range from beginners needing basic orientation to experienced fishermen looking to maximize the capabilities of advanced sonar and GPS systems. about:
Certified Parts Corporation (CPC) was founded in 1982 by James Grafft in Edgerton, Wisconsin. The company traces its roots to 1974 when Grafft worked at Fox Corporation in Janesville and recognized the need for continuous parts supply for manufacturers that had ceased operations. In 1976 he purchased Fox's service-parts division and the Bridgestone brand on his 26th birthday. Two years later, Grafft established CPC with a mission to preserve well-known international and local legacy brands facing extinction, beginning with the acquisition of Arctic Cat's snowmobile division, including tooling, dies, intellectual property and trademarks.

Today CPC operates a 200,000-square-foot factory in Edgerton where it manufactures original service parts — carburetors, the full line of Comet torque converters and clutches, and other components — for a portfolio that includes Comet, TecumsehPower, Wisconsin Wagon, and vintage recreational-vehicle brands. The company also owns historic motorcycle and mini-cycle marques such as Bridgestone, Indian, Rupp, Chaparral and Steen, and supplies hard-to-find engine parts for snowmobiles and mini-cycles. Production volumes support both OEM contracts and aftermarket distribution through a worldwide dealer network.

CPC serves OEM manufacturers in the recreational, construction, agricultural and marine sectors, as well as dealers and end users maintaining vintage equipment. Its customer base includes original equipment builders that integrate Comet clutches into new products and a global service network that supports TecumsehPower, Lauson and Snow King engines.

The business was built on a passion for history and an eye for opportunity: Grafft's strategy of acquiring orphaned brands, restarting production and re-establishing dealer channels has returned multiple legacy names to active manufacturing.

Corona adapted her aunt's salsa macha recipe in her Boise kitchen, launching a line of nut- and chile-based salsas that blend Veracruz and Oaxaca traditions with African influences.

The company produces salsa macha in varieties including peanut and cranberry, using ingredients such as seeds, nuts, chiles, olive oil, and dried fruit. Production takes place in a Boise kitchen facility; the Mexico-based family operation employs 50 people and supplies thousands of Mexican families weekly, though Chicana Foods' own headcount and facility size are not disclosed. Chicana Foods sells through specialty grocers, coffee shops, farmers markets, delis, wineries, and museum stores across Idaho and Utah. The founders frame the business as an extension of family, prioritizing a living wage and safe workplace for employees. A portion of sales supports the Stay-In-School Quinceañera Program, which exposes Latine middle-school students to Latine art, literature, and culture. This social mission, coupled with the use of high-quality, small-batch ingredients, is presented as the company's distinguishing approach.

name: Clearloop Corporation
old_description: Clearloop was founded as a carbon solution by three Tennesseans who want to ensure that the environmental, health, and economic benefits of clean energy reach the communities that need them the most, beginning in our own backyard.
about:
Clearloop Corporation is based in Nashville, Tennessee. The company was founded as a carbon solution by three Tennesseans — Bob Corney, Laura Zapata, and Gov. Phil Bredesen — who wanted the environmental, health, and economic benefits of clean energy to reach communities that need them most, starting in their own region. Clearloop was later acquired by Silicon Ranch, one of the largest independent power producers in the United States, to deliver on that promise at scale.

The company develops carbon solutions that help organizations measure their emissions, reclaim them by building new solar capacity in the most carbon-intense parts of the U.S. electricity grid, and track the resulting clean energy generation. Rather than purchasing power from existing projects, Clearloop finances and facilitates the development of new solar installations in locations such as Arcadia, Louisiana; Jackson, Tennessee; Panola County, Mississippi; Paris, Tennessee; and White Pine, Tennessee. Their model charges partners a fee based on a percentage of the product or corporate carbon footprint, directing those funds into new solar construction.

Clearloop works with companies of all sizes, from global corporations to small businesses and educational institutions, that want to offset their carbon footprint and expand access to clean energy. Partners receive a "100% reclaimed carbon footprint®" certification for products or services tied to the investment. The firm focuses on the U.S. South, where grid carbon intensity is highest, arguing that building solar there displaces more fossil-fuel generation per watt than in cleaner regions.

The founders started Clearloop as outsiders to corporate sustainability with a pragmatic, optimistic approach to climate action. They aim to green the U.S. electricity grid by 2050 by turning everyday purchases and corporate commitments into new renewable energy projects that benefit underserved communities. The company emphasizes equal access, low-risk long-term investment, corporate accountability, and scalable commitment as core principles.

Rainbow is working diligently to capitalize on innovative technologies so future generations have reliable and sustainable energy solutions.
about:
Rainbow Energy Center, LLC (REC) acquired Coal Creek Station, a coal-fired power plant near Underwood, North Dakota, on May 1, 2022. The acquisition included the plant's generation assets and approximately 200 employees. REC's sister company, Nexus Line, LLC, simultaneously purchased the high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission line that carries power from the station to the Dickinson converter station near Buffalo, Minnesota. The ownership structure places both entities under common leadership focused on efficient energy production and sound energy management.

The company operates Coal Creek Station as a baseload generation facility while also pursuing wind energy development and carbon capture initiatives. REC describes its portfolio as spanning generation, transmission, wind, and carbon capture, aiming to harness natural resources for a sustainable future.

Electricity from Coal Creek Station serves residential, commercial, and industrial customers across the region. The company emphasizes local procurement, citing Captain's Cabin, a vendor in the Underwood area, as an example of its commitment to keeping business within the community. REC states that its wages and spending help fuel the local economy.

REC positions itself as a provider of reliable, affordable, and increasingly clean energy. Its stated mission centers on safety, environmental consciousness, and improving the lives of community members through integrity and accountability. The company highlights the plant's efficiency and its investments in carbon capture as differentiators in the transition to cleaner energy.

old_description: Coastal Power Systems is an engineering-driven manufacturer of critical electrical infrastructure. about:
Coastal Power Systems operates from Tomball, Texas, in the Houston metropolitan area. The company was founded in 1995 as a supplier of industrial circuit breakers and has since expanded into a full-service provider of electrical power distribution solutions.

The firm manufactures custom power distribution equipment including UL 1558 switchgear, UL 891 switchboards, UL 67 panelboards, and medium- and low-voltage switchgear, along with protection and control systems. Its capabilities span engineering and design studies (coordination, arc flash, short circuit), NETA-guided testing and commissioning, preventive maintenance, circuit breaker restoration, switchgear modernization, arc flash mitigation, and 24/7 emergency response. Field services cover primary and secondary injection testing, protective relay testing, equipment repair, and refurbishment. The company also supplies new, reconditioned, and obsolete industrial circuit breakers with retrofit kits and parts.

Coastal Power Systems serves utilities, data centers, power generation facilities, oil and gas operations, petrochemical plants, industrial manufacturers, water and wastewater systems, transportation infrastructure, commercial buildings, and renewable energy sites. Its customers include EPC firms, consulting engineers, and mission-critical operators who require single-source responsibility for electrical infrastructure from design through lifecycle support.

The company emphasizes an integrated model that combines engineering, manufacturing, field service, testing, repair, and modernization under one roof. Its stated mission is to deliver dependable, responsive, and practical power solutions that improve reliability, reduce downtime, and support long-term performance of critical electrical infrastructure. The tagline "We Build What We Sell. We Support What We Build." reflects this end-to-end approach.

It credits its ability to stay nimble during the pandemic, as highlighted in a 2020 Meat + Poultry magazine feature, to its family-led management and dedication to time-honored recipes and the finest ingredients.

name: Colonial Wire & Cable of NJ
old_description: Since 1944, Colonial Wire and Cable has served the electrical distribution market with quality products, superior customer service and, like the Minutemen, prompt response and short-lead times. And all our wire and cable products are proudly made in the USA.
about:
Colonial Wire & Cable of NJ traces its roots to 1944 in Edison, New Jersey, where it began as a family-owned enterprise. Now in its third generation, the company remains family-run, with ownership and daily operations kept within the founding family. The name and operating philosophy draw inspiration from the Colonial Minutemen, symbolizing rapid deployment and immediate response.

The company operates two manufacturing facilities: a residential cable and wiring plant in Hauppauge, New York, and a commercial wire and cable facility in Edison, New Jersey. Both produce copper electrical building wire for commercial, industrial, and residential applications. All products are made in the United States, and the company maintains an extensive inventory to support high fill rates and quick turnaround.

Colonial Wire & Cable sells exclusively through electrical distributors and wholesalers across North America. Its customer base includes contractors and specifiers serving commercial construction, industrial maintenance, and residential building projects. The company emphasizes direct manufacturer-to-distributor relationships, eliminating intermediate layers.

The Minutemen-inspired ethos drives a focus on prompt response and short lead times. Quality assurance is anchored by Underwriters Laboratory (UL) approval across more than 30 safety standards, with UL verification programs that include unannounced factory inspections and follow-up testing. The company also aligns with industry standards from ASTM, ICEA, IEEE, NEMA, NFPA, and the National Electrical Code.

old_description: Mica capacitors hold an important place in RF engineering due to their stable performance and long-term reliability. These components use natural mica as the dielectric, which supports accurate capacitance values with minimal drift. In high-frequency designs, small variations can change circuit behavior, so engineers look for parts that protect performance.
about:
Commercial Radio Company, Inc. operates from Cavendish, Vermont, where it was founded in 1970 by engineer Dan Churchill. Churchill, known for his hands-on troubleshooting on transmitting towers, built the business around distributing Cornell-Dubilier mica capacitors. Today the company remains a second-generation family enterprise focused on supplying mica capacitors for emerging semiconductor applications.

The firm acts as a stocking distributor for the full Cornell-Dubilier mica capacitor line, including Types 271, 272, 273, 291, 292, 293, 294, and the HT, HK, AT, and AK series. Its inventory spans thousands of part numbers — such as NL523W02-004, NL523W03-010, and 29280B242JO0 — all held in stock for immediate shipment. The company emphasizes rapid fulfillment, with a team available across multiple time zones to accelerate order processing.

Customers span aerospace and defense, medical equipment, counter-drone systems, electronic warfare, wind and solar power, electric-vehicle charging infrastructure, military programs, and broadcast radio stations. The capacitors are specified in high-frequency RF designs where stable capacitance and minimal drift are critical.

Commercial Radio Company differentiates itself by maintaining what it describes as the largest U.S. inventory of Cornell-Dubilier mica capacitors, offering competitive pricing backed by a price-match guarantee, and supplying U.S.-made components that avoid tariffs. The founder’s original commitment to hands-on technical support continues through a round-the-clock service model.

about:
Complete Cable Company LLC is a family-owned manufacturer of custom wire harnesses and cable assemblies based in St. Joseph, Michigan. The company is led by co-owners Rob Kasun and Jon Kasun, who oversee business operations, production, and quality execution. Founded as a Michigan-based operation, the business focuses on build-to-print manufacturing for OEM customers.

The company produces wire harnesses and cable assemblies from prototype through repeat production, handling wire cutting, stripping, crimping, and assembly for gauges ranging from 14 to 22 AWG with PVC and SRPVC insulation. Contraxx emphasizes its distributed manufacturing system as a differentiator, enabling efficient production, dependable timelines, and seamless execution at any scale. The company was founded on the belief that furniture manufacturing jobs should stay in America, and it highlights made-exclusively-in-America production, custom design flexibility, turnkey installation, on-site field measurements, and time-critical delivery as core value propositions.

It remains a public, nonprofit entity governed by a local board, with all revenues reinvested in the community.

The corporation delivers a full suite of utility and telecommunications services: electric distribution, water treatment and distribution, wastewater collection and treatment, cable video, high‑speed internet over a fiber‑coax network, digital voice, and security and automation. It also runs a solar energy program and an IPTV streaming product, ConwayCorpTV. Crews work 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, maintaining substations, treatment plants, and a geographic information system that maps the infrastructure.

Customers are residential and commercial users within the Conway service territory. The utility serves households, local businesses, and municipal facilities, providing both basic utility needs and advanced broadband and entertainment packages.

The founding charter tied the organization directly to community well‑being, a mission reiterated in its core values of customer satisfaction, innovation, safety, reliability, responsibility, and community engagement. Profits are directed back into infrastructure upgrades, education initiatives, and economic development rather than distributed to shareholders.

The founders’ original focus on problem-solving remains central: Craftco positions itself as a manufacturing partner that combines engineering, machining, fabrication, and assembly to solve complex challenges.
